# Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 Summary

The 1997 Conservative Party manifesto, entitled "You Can Only Be Sure with the Conservatives," presents their case for re-election after 18 years in government. The document argues that Conservative policies transformed Britain from "the sick man of Europe" into its most successful economy, with restored industrial peace, reduced trade union power, and increased enterprise.

## Economic Vision

The manifesto positions Britain as "the Enterprise Centre of Europe," highlighting achievements including six consecutive years of faster growth than France and Germany, the lowest unemployment among major European economies, and the largest share of European inward investment. The Conservatives pledge to maintain tight spending control, aiming to reduce government spending below 40% of national income, achieve a 20p basic income tax rate, and keep inflation at 2.5% or below.

The party firmly opposes the European Social Chapter and any national minimum wage, arguing these would destroy jobs by burdening businesses with costs that have increased European unemployment by 4.5 million.

## Ownership and Opportunity

Central to the manifesto is expanding personal ownership and family support. Key proposals include allowing non-working spouses to transfer their tax allowance to working partners with caring responsibilities, providing young workers with personal pension funds through national insurance rebates, and creating a partnership scheme for long-term care costs. The Conservatives celebrate their achievements in home ownership (up 4.7 million since 1979) and share ownership (10 million shareholders).

## Public Services and Education

The manifesto promises to increase real NHS spending annually, expand primary care services, and maintain targets for waiting times. In education, it proposes publishing all school test results, creating specialist schools, allowing schools greater selection powers, and establishing grammar schools where parents desire them.

## Law and Order

The document advocates tough anti-crime measures including minimum sentences for persistent offenders, expanded CCTV coverage, tackling juvenile crime through parental control orders, and abolishing automatic early release from prison.

## Constitutional Position

The Conservatives firmly oppose Scottish and Welsh devolution, proportional representation, and further European integration. They promise a referendum before any single currency membership and pledge to protect Britain's opt-outs from European social legislation while defending national sovereignty and parliamentary supremacy.
